title: Python: duplicate imports of the same symbol are one binding for known-class binding from an annotation (DEC-303 (a93) item 1)
description: Accepted hold task for rich misses 5.7 (rich/rule.py:66) and 5.8 (rich/table.py:491), classified under DEC-303 (a92) item 3 and ruled by (a93) item 1. Measured at dev dce9e90: a module that imports the same class name twice suppresses known-class binding from the annotation, even though both imports bind the same class; rule.py imports Console at line 3 (relative) and 118 (absolute, in its __main__ demo), table.py at 18-25 (TYPE_CHECKING) and 929 (absolute). Ruling: duplicate imports of the SAME symbol become one binding. Fixtures cover 5.7's __main__ shape and 5.8's closure read. Refused twins must still refuse: two imports binding DIFFERENT symbols, an import followed by a non-import rebinding, and a conditional import of a different symbol. Mutants observed red. Two rounds; every created and removed in-repo edge on the five-pin corpus is listed to opum-doc before the clear. Runs after GCLI-151 in the leader's order and is not started until briefed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A module that imports the same class twice (relative and absolute, in any scope) resolves an annotated receiver method call to the class method; fixtures cover the 5.7 __main__ shape and the 5.8 closure read
Two imports binding different symbols, an import followed by a non-import rebinding, and a conditional import of a different symbol all stay unresolved, with fixtures and mutants observed red
Every in-repo edge created or removed on the five-pin corpus is listed to opum-doc before the clear
